source.paraphrase: Interaction declarations and graph metadata must match the owned application contract. A declaration or diagram must not be treated as proof that an effect occurred or that an architecture rule was satisfied.

invariants.why: Interaction declarations and graph metadata must match the owned application contract. A declaration or diagram must not be treated as proof that an effect occurred or that an architecture rule was satisfied. The product declares interactions or uses dependency information or a graph as architecture evidence.
invariants.fixHint: Compare declared and actual registered interactions with a bounded application test. Keep declared, observed and omitted behavior distinct. Test the actual metadata ownership policy: snapshots copy top-level collections but can retain nested metadata references. Validate and redact labels and metadata before sharing them. source.paraphrase: A graph consumer must verify the returned graph and own timeout and readiness failures. A matching request identifier must not be treated as authenticated response provenance.

invariants.why: A graph consumer must verify the returned graph and own timeout and readiness failures. A matching request identifier must not be treated as authenticated response provenance. The product calls requestGraph or supplies observability buses, handlers or engine lifecycle controls.

source.paraphrase: The inspector must remain an explicitly admitted development diagnostic. Access to its recording, commands and graph endpoints must be protected independently of CORS and the production environment flag.

invariants.why: The inspector must remain an explicitly admitted development diagnostic. Access to its recording, commands and graph endpoints must be protected independently of CORS and the production environment flag. The product starts or exposes the dcouplr inspector.

source.paraphrase: Inspection data must have an explicit redaction, serialization, ownership and retention policy before capture or export. An event-count limit must not be treated as a byte budget.

invariants.why: Inspection data must have an explicit redaction, serialization, ownership and retention policy before capture or export. An event-count limit must not be treated as a byte budget. The product captures, exports or shares diagnostic events.

source.paraphrase: An inspector owner must await close and verify cleanup on successful startup, failed startup and shutdown. A failed bind must not be assumed to remove an observer created before listening.

invariants.why: An inspector owner must await close and verify cleanup on successful startup, failed startup and shutdown. A failed bind must not be assumed to remove an observer created before listening. The product owns an inspector server or retries its startup.
